pool.title: Cowboy Bebop
pool.synopsis: Four bounty hunters and a dog work the solar system for money they immediately lose, and each of them is running from something they will eventually have to stop running from.

pool.title: Steins;Gate
pool.synopsis: A self-styled mad scientist discovers he can send text messages into the past, and spends the second half of the show undoing what he did in the first.

pool.title: Sousou no Frieren
pool.synopsis: The elf who helped kill the demon king outlives the party that did it with her, and sets out to learn, far too late, what her friends were.

pool.title: Odd Taxi
pool.synopsis: A walrus drives a taxi through a city where a girl has gone missing, and every fare he picks up turns out to be one thread of the same knot.

pool.title: Planetes
pool.synopsis: The crew that clears orbital debris for a living get the jobs nobody photographs, and the show takes their careers as seriously as its physics.

picks.title: Cowboy Bebop
picks.case: You have Cowboy Bebop on your plan-to-watch list already and there is no reason to wait. It is episodic, so it costs you one twenty-minute session to find out whether you like it, and the arc underneath the episodes only sharpens on a rewatch. Start here rather than with anything longer.

picks.title: Planetes
picks.case: Both things on your list are science fiction, so this is the third one worth knowing about. It shares Cowboy Bebop's lived-in, unglamorous space and its interest in people whose jobs are beneath the notice of the setting they live in. Where Steins;Gate escalates, Planetes stays at ground level and gets its weight from that.

picks.title: Odd Taxi
picks.case: If the reason Steins;Gate is on your list is the slow reveal that everything was connected, this does the same thing in thirteen episodes and does it with a much lighter touch. It is a mystery told almost entirely in conversations in a car. It is also the shortest thing here, which makes it a good second pick alongside Cowboy Bebop.
